input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 itself meets the preferred position: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid Fees, and Vendor is expressly denied a reciprocal convenience right during a committed term. However, Section 2.1 imposes a three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights," which directly contradicts and would gut the Section 9.4 convenience right (and any refund) for the committed volume. The order-of-precedence clause (2.2) does not resolve an internal conflict between two Agreement sections, so the ambiguity is a high-severity deviation in a multi-year term. The minimal fix conforms 2.1 to preserve the Section 9.4 right and reduce the commitment pro rata on permitted termination.

ops.oldText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: on a take-or-pay basis; provided that this commitment does not limit Customer's termination or reduction rights under this Agreement, including Section 9.4, and is reduced pro rata for any Services terminated.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9.4 correctly gives us a 30-day convenience termination with a pro-rata refund, but Section 2.1's "without reduction or termination rights" language would negate it for the three-year committed volume. We have conformed 2.1 so the minimum commitment reduces pro rata on any permitted termination, preserving the bargain in Section 9.4.
proposal.summary: Carve termination/reduction rights out of the take-or-pay commitment in 2.1 so the Customer convenience right in 9.4 remains effective.
